correctness.rationale: Define Q_{ell,h}(u) as the exact symmetric product; its positivity proves derivative reduction. A cubic P has three simple positive roots by integer sign changes in disjoint intervals and degree bound, giving four intervals of strict midpoint local type. At L=14, derivative H/(5Q1Q10) has exactly two positive roots (bracketed and Descartes). Endpoint derivatives exclude boundary minima. A strict exact rational comparison of log-loss at x=1 versus x=7 makes the center nonglobal; symmetry and the exhaustive stationary classification give precisely two global asymmetric locations. The one-scale derivative has exactly one sign change and excludes the metastable-center phenomenon. The runnable CHECK.py tests derivative identities and integer inequalities but finite checks do not replace continuum proof.

value.rationale: The question models a motivated reserve-connection planning conflict: one stepping-stone must serve two species with widely different movement ranges. The exact three-switch stability law, strict metastability of central placement, and complete rational L=14 global classification reveal a meaningful failure of center-first optimization despite each single scale individually excluding the phenomenon. The result is not just computation of a random parameter: it separates multi-species geometric-mean design from one-species optimality and gives robust, reproducible algebraic phase behavior. There is no claim of field-calibrated effect.
